## Natural history notes

A small acrobat ant characterized by its dark reddish-brown to black body, heart-shaped abdomen, and habit of raising the abdomen over the body when disturbed. In Florida, it is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, yards, and areas with trees, shrubs, dead wood, or plant cavities for nesting. It forages on vegetation and bark for small insects, nectar, honeydew, and other sugary resources, while nesting in twigs, hollow stems, dead branches, or other small cavities and serving as prey for spiders, birds, lizards, and other insect-eating animals.
